markerNote: Counts are case-sensitive and are taken from the built artifact. They are assertions about what the BUNDLE contains, not about the source tree: this build is not minified, so comments ship. A surviving `gemini` in a comment is not Google support, and a surviving api id is expected even after removal because pi-ai's compat registry names every api factory (the removed one is replaced by a stub that throws a readable error). Read them together with the module table in the bundle-size record.
notes: After revision: c6b99e7, tree fa4d502deef73e7b362c66f070e9be7d31a6a95f, identical to pre-rebase 1f29a77 (same tree hash), so the artifact built before the rebase is this revision's build; it was also rebuilt here and came out byte-identical (sha256 87D4B012FC0DDDFAE2FFCE642E04B59EEBAC73A140F9A1A82E3642C635F2A42A).

ACCURATE CLAIM: no Google IMPLEMENTATION is bundled. @google/genai=0, @google/generative-ai=0, generativelanguage=0, 'Gemini API'=0, '// node_modules/@google/'=0. It is NOT true that the string appears nowhere: the build is unminified so comments ship. The single capital-G 'Gemini' is pi-ai's own comment '// Google (Gemini)' in node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/utils/overflow.js above a generic context-overflow regex (/maximum prompt length is \\d+/i) - third-party, not ours. The four lowercase 'gemini' are our own removal-documenting comments: src/mcp/types.ts (why 'openai' is now the factory default) and src/services/model-service.ts (why the default: branch stays a runtime safety net for types pruned from disk).

The 4 remaining occurrences of the string 'google-generative-ai' are the replacement STUB, not support: pi-ai's compat registry calls every api factory, so the id must still be named; the stubbed factory throws 'Baizer does not bundle the google-generative-ai api implementation' (530 B in the bundle, vs 14,258 B for the real module before).
